activities.title: Mass, moles & particles
activities.description: Connect macroscopic mass to mole amount and microscopic particle counts.
activities.limits: Pure substance; the particle identity must be specified. Formula units and molecules are not interchangeable.
activities.goal: Explain how equal mole amounts can have different masses.

activities.title: Isotopes & average atomic mass
activities.description: Change an isotope abundance and distinguish atomic mass from mass number.
activities.limits: Two-isotope teaching mixture; isotope masses are entered, not inferred from integer mass numbers.
activities.goal: Explain why the average need not be an integer or the mass of any one atom.

activities.title: Electron configuration & ions
activities.description: Fill occupied subshells through calcium and compare neutral atoms with ions.
activities.limits: Ground-state Aufbau filling through 20 electrons. No transition-metal exceptions; subshell boxes are symbolic, not electron trajectories.
activities.goal: Distinguish changes in electron number from changes in nuclear identity.

activities.title: Photoelectron spectroscopy
activities.description: Compare symbolic shell peaks and occupied-electron intensities.
activities.equation: Photon energy = binding energy + electron kinetic energy
activities.limits: Illustrative shell binding positions, not measured spectra. Peak area represents electron count within this simplified display.
activities.goal: Use peak position and area for different kinds of evidence.

activities.title: Photon energy & wavelength
activities.description: Connect electromagnetic wavelength, frequency and photon energy.
activities.limits: Monochromatic light; photons have energy but this model does not calculate absorption probabilities.
activities.goal: Explain the inverse wavelength–energy relationship.

activities.title: Ionic attraction & distance
activities.description: Explore the inverse-distance energy of two point charges.
activities.limits: Point-charge energy in vacuum; actual lattice enthalpy sums many interactions and includes repulsion.
activities.goal: Compare charge magnitude and separation without equating pair energy to lattice enthalpy.

activities.title: VSEPR geometry & lone pairs
activities.description: Change electron domains and distinguish electron geometry from molecular geometry.
activities.equation: Electron-domain geometry depends on domain count; molecular geometry depends on atom positions.
activities.limits: Ideal domain model. A multiple bond counts as one domain; real bond angles depend on the molecule.
activities.goal: Explain why tetrahedral electron geometry does not always mean tetrahedral molecular geometry.

activities.title: Lewis structures & formal charge
activities.description: Account for assigned electrons without treating formal charge as measured partial charge.
activities.limits: One atom in a proposed Lewis structure. This does not validate the total molecular electron count or octet.
activities.goal: Use charge bookkeeping alongside total electrons, resonance and bonding.

activities.title: Bond dipoles & molecular polarity
activities.description: Compare symmetry and cancellation for common ideal molecular geometries.
activities.equation: Molecular dipole = vector sum of bond dipoles
activities.limits: Ideal geometry and identical bond dipoles within each example. Relative values are schematic, not measured debye.
activities.goal: Explain why polar bonds can occur in a nonpolar molecule.

activities.title: Ideal gases
activities.description: Manipulate gas amount, temperature and volume while preserving units.
activities.limits: Ideal gas behavior; intermolecular interactions and finite particle volume are omitted.
activities.goal: Explain why pressure depends on absolute temperature.

activities.title: Gas mixtures & partial pressures
activities.description: Connect component amount to mole fraction and partial pressure.
activities.limits: Ideal, nonreacting mixture. Composition changes do not imply any specified container mechanics.
activities.goal: Distinguish mole fraction from a mass fraction.

activities.title: Kinetic molecular theory
activities.description: Compare ideal-gas speed distributions for different molar masses.
activities.limits: Maxwell–Boltzmann ideal-gas distribution; M must be kg/mol in the speed equation.
activities.goal: Explain why equal-temperature gases share average kinetic energy rather than equal speed.

activities.title: Solutions & dilution
activities.description: Conserve solute amount when changing solution volume.
activities.limits: Volumes describe final solution volume, not water added; no solute loss or reaction.
activities.goal: Explain how concentration changes while solute amount remains constant.

activities.title: Spectrophotometry & Beer–Lambert law
activities.description: Relate concentration and optical path to absorbance and transmittance.
activities.limits: Monochromatic, dilute solution with constant absorptivity; scattering and instrument saturation are omitted.
activities.goal: Explain why absorbance is linear in concentration but transmittance is not.

activities.title: Limiting reactants & reaction extent
activities.description: Track consumption and formation in a supplied balanced coefficient ratio.
activities.equation: Maximum extent ξ = min(nA/a, nB/b); product = cξ
activities.limits: The entered coefficients must belong to an actually balanced reaction; this ratio model cannot infer elemental formulas.
activities.goal: Explain why the smaller initial amount is not necessarily the limiting reactant.

activities.title: Theoretical, actual & percent yield
activities.description: Distinguish stoichiometric prediction from measured recovery.
activities.limits: A value above 100% can signal wet or impure product, an incorrect theoretical yield or measurement error.
activities.goal: Explain why high percent yield alone does not establish purity.

activities.title: Net ionic reactions
activities.description: Separate reacting ions from spectators in precipitation and neutralization.
activities.equation: Net ionic equations conserve both atoms and total charge.
activities.limits: Canonical aqueous examples; solubility equilibria and reagent exhaustion are not dynamically simulated.
activities.goal: Explain which species change and why spectators cancel.

activities.title: Redox & electron accounting
activities.description: Connect metal oxidation to transferred electrons.
activities.equation: Electrons lost in oxidation equal electrons gained in reduction.
activities.limits: Selected half-reactions only; full reaction feasibility requires a coupled reduction and conditions.
activities.goal: Explain why electron amount depends on the oxidation-state change.

activities.title: Rate laws & reaction order
activities.description: Manipulate independently specified empirical orders.
activities.limits: Empirical orders need not equal overall stoichiometric coefficients. k units are M^(1−m−n)/s.
activities.goal: Explain why changing concentration can have different rate effects for different orders.

activities.title: Initial-rate evidence
activities.description: Infer an order from trials that hold other reactants constant.
activities.limits: One reactant varied; temperature, catalyst and other concentrations remain constant. Measurement uncertainty is omitted.
activities.goal: Explain why both ratios are needed to infer order.

activities.title: Integrated rate laws & half-life
activities.description: Compare zero-, first- and second-order single-reactant decay.
activities.equation: Zero: A=A₀−kt; first: A=A₀e^(−kt); second: A=A₀/(1+kA₀t)
activities.limits: Single-reactant irreversible model. Zero-order decay is stopped at depletion. The rate-constant units change with order.
activities.goal: Compare how half-life depends on starting concentration.

activities.title: Activation energy & temperature
activities.description: Explore the exponential dependence of a model rate constant on temperature.
activities.limits: Arrhenius parameters are constant; the model is not an elementary collision simulation.
activities.goal: Explain how lowering Ea differs from making ΔG more negative.

activities.title: Calorimetry & reaction heat
activities.description: Account for solution heating and the opposite heat sign for a reaction.
activities.limits: Adiabatic simplified calorimeter; vessel heat capacity and heat loss are omitted.
activities.goal: Explain the sign of reaction heat when the solution warms.

activities.title: Heating curves & phase changes
activities.description: Allocate energy to heating ice, melting and warming water at 1 atm.
activities.equation: q = mcΔT within a phase; q = mL during a phase change
activities.limits: Pure water at 1 atm, cice=2.09 and cwater=4.18 J/g/°C, fusion=334 J/g. View stops at 100 °C; boiling is not modeled.
activities.goal: Explain why temperature can stay constant while energy is supplied.

activities.title: Hess’s law
activities.description: Scale and reverse supplied reaction steps and sum their enthalpies.
activities.limits: Energy bookkeeping only. You must also combine chemical equations and cancel intermediates correctly.
activities.goal: Explain why reversing a step reverses its enthalpy sign.

activities.title: Bond enthalpy estimates
activities.description: Compare energy to break bonds with energy released forming bonds.
activities.limits: Average gas-phase bond enthalpies are estimates, not exact reaction enthalpies in every phase.
activities.goal: Explain why breaking bonds requires energy rather than releasing it.

activities.title: ICE equilibrium: A ⇌ B
activities.description: Find an equilibrium composition from conservation and an entered Kc.
activities.limits: Ideal 1:1 closed system with fixed volume and temperature. No reaction rates are predicted.
activities.goal: Explain why equilibrium does not require equal concentrations.

activities.title: Reaction quotient & direction
activities.description: Compare Q to K for A + B ⇌ C before equilibrium is reached.
activities.equation: Qc = [C]/([A][B]); Q<K favors net forward change
activities.limits: Activities approximated by concentrations relative to 1 M; direction does not imply a rate or exact extent.
activities.goal: Explain why Q and K have the same expression but different roles.

activities.title: Solubility & common ions
activities.description: Calculate a 1:1 salt’s equilibrium solubility in the presence of a common ion.
activities.limits: Ideal AB salt; no complex formation, acid–base chemistry or activity-coefficient corrections.
activities.goal: Explain why a common ion lowers solubility without changing Ksp at fixed temperature.

activities.title: Compression & equilibrium
activities.description: Solve an ideal N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ equilibrium after changing volume.
activities.limits: Fixed-temperature ideal concentration model; actual industrial kinetics, heat release and nonideal gas effects are omitted.
activities.goal: Explain why changing volume changes equilibrium composition but not K at fixed temperature.

activities.title: Strong acids & bases
activities.description: Connect analytical concentration to pH including water autoionization.
activities.limits: Fully dissociated monoprotic acid or monovalent strong base; ideal dilute concentration approximation.
activities.goal: Explain why an extremely dilute acid approaches pH 7 rather than becoming basic.

activities.title: Weak-acid equilibrium
activities.description: Solve charge and mass balance instead of assuming all acid dissociates.
activities.equation: Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA]; charge and mass balances constrain the solution
activities.limits: Ideal monoprotic acid at 25 °C; includes water autoionization. No polyprotic or activity corrections.
activities.goal: Explain the difference between acid strength and acid concentration.

activities.title: Buffer composition
activities.description: Explore a buffer ratio while separating pH from buffer capacity.
activities.limits: Henderson–Hasselbalch approximation using supplied concentrations. Does not directly calculate buffer capacity or titration reactions.
activities.goal: Explain why two buffers with the same ratio can resist added acid differently.

activities.title: Weak-acid/strong-base titration
activities.description: Solve pH throughout a titration, including the equivalence region.
activities.limits: Ideal monoprotic acid titrated with monovalent strong base at 25 °C. Constant volumes are additive; water autoionization is included.
activities.goal: Explain why weak-acid equivalence is not generally pH 7.

activities.title: Entropy, enthalpy & Gibbs energy
activities.description: Separate favorable direction from reaction speed and explore temperature dependence.
activities.limits: Thermodynamic parameters held constant with temperature; a favorable sign does not specify reaction rate.
activities.goal: Explain how temperature can change favorability when ΔH and ΔS have the same sign.

activities.title: Standard Gibbs energy & equilibrium
activities.description: Connect a standard free-energy difference to an equilibrium constant.
activities.limits: K is dimensionless with defined standard states. ΔG° is not ΔG for every current composition.
activities.goal: Explain why a large K need not imply that a reaction is fast.

activities.title: Galvanic cells & Nernst equation
activities.description: Compare standard potential with a nonstandard reaction quotient.
activities.limits: Ideal activity approximation at 25 °C; no overpotential, resistance or electrode kinetics.
activities.goal: Explain why spontaneous cell direction depends on current composition.

activities.title: Electrolysis & Faraday’s law
activities.description: Account for current, time, electrons and deposited metal mass.
activities.limits: 100% current efficiency; side reactions and electrode surface effects are omitted.
activities.goal: Explain why equal charge can deposit different metal masses.

activities.title: Periodic trends & effective attraction
activities.description: Compare qualitative atomic-radius and ionization-energy tendencies within selected periods.
activities.equation: Across a period, increasing nuclear charge generally strengthens effective attraction on valence electrons.
activities.limits: Trend explorer, not a numerical radius or ionization-energy predictor; subshell and pairing exceptions matter.
activities.goal: Explain a trend using shielding, shell and nuclear charge rather than just a memorized direction.

activities.title: Bond energy & separation
activities.description: Compare attractive bonding near equilibrium with short-distance repulsion.
activities.limits: Illustrative diatomic potential, not measured molecular data. Minimum energy at r0; dissociation approaches zero at large r.
activities.goal: Explain why both too-close and too-far separations differ from the energy minimum.

activities.title: Intermolecular forces & properties
activities.description: Compare structural evidence for hydrogen bonding, dipole attractions and dispersion.
activities.equation: All molecules exhibit dispersion; additional attractions depend on structure.
activities.limits: Qualitative examples. Boiling points also depend on size, shape and pressure; this tool does not predict a measured value.
activities.goal: Explain a property using actual molecular interactions.

activities.title: Reaction mechanisms & rate-determining steps
activities.description: Compare an elementary step with an overall reaction.
activities.equation: An elementary A+B step has a rate proportional to [A][B]; a multistep overall reaction requires mechanism analysis.
activities.limits: Two qualitative mechanism examples, not fitted kinetic data. A slow-step expression may need intermediate elimination.
activities.goal: Explain why an overall coefficient does not generally determine reaction order.

activities.title: Catalysis & reaction energy
activities.description: Change a reaction barrier while preserving the reactant-to-product energy difference.
activities.equation: Catalysts lower activation barriers without changing reaction ΔG or equilibrium K.
activities.limits: Illustrative reaction-coordinate curves, not measured energy surfaces. Both barriers must lie above both endpoints.
activities.goal: Explain why faster forward and reverse reactions do not shift the equilibrium constant.

activities.title: Temperature & equilibrium constant
activities.description: Explore the van ’t Hoff relation for a fixed reaction enthalpy.
activities.limits: Constant ΔH° approximation; quantitative van ’t Hoff calculation is an introductory-college extension of AP equilibrium reasoning.
activities.goal: Explain why temperature can change K while concentration changes at fixed temperature do not.

activities.title: Indicators & transition ranges
activities.description: Relate solution pH to protonated and deprotonated indicator fractions.
activities.limits: Ideal single-equilibrium indicator; colors are illustrative and actual visibility depends on concentration and observation.
activities.goal: Explain why an indicator transition spans a range rather than one exact pH.
